title: Network security controls: processes and roles
summary: Security policies and operational procedures for network security controls are documented, in use and known; roles and responsibilities are assigned.
typical_evidence: Network security policy; RACI for network controls

title: Network security controls configured and maintained
summary: NSC configuration standards; change control for network connections and NSC changes; accurate network and data-flow diagrams; ports and services justified; NSC rulesets reviewed at least every six months.
typical_evidence: Network diagram; CDE data-flow diagram; firewall or security group rule export; six-monthly rule review record

title: Network access to and from the CDE restricted
summary: Inbound and outbound CDE traffic limited to what is necessary; wireless networks separated from the CDE.
typical_evidence: Security group or firewall rules for CDE; segmentation evidence

title: Connections between trusted and untrusted networks controlled
summary: NSCs between trusted and untrusted networks; inbound traffic only to authorised publicly accessible services; anti-spoofing; no CHD storage reachable from untrusted networks; internal IPs not disclosed.
typical_evidence: DMZ or public subnet design; ingress rules

title: Risks from devices connecting to both untrusted networks and the CDE
summary: Security controls on computing devices (including employee-owned) that connect to untrusted networks and the CDE so they cannot be altered by users.
typical_evidence: Endpoint firewall or MDM policy; device configuration export

title: Secure configuration: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for secure configuration are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Configuration management policy

title: System components configured and managed securely
summary: Configuration standards based on industry hardening guidance; vendor defaults changed or disabled; one primary function per server; only necessary services; insecure services secured; non-console admin access encrypted.
typical_evidence: Hardening standards (CIS benchmarks); configuration scan results; evidence default accounts disabled

title: Wireless environments configured securely
summary: Wireless vendor defaults changed; wireless keys changed on personnel change or suspected compromise.
typical_evidence: Wireless configuration (only if wireless connects to the CDE)

title: Protect stored account data: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for protecting stored account data are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Data protection policy covering CHD

title: Storage of account data kept to a minimum
summary: Data retention and disposal policies limit storage to what is needed with a quarterly process to delete data past retention.
typical_evidence: CHD data retention policy; quarterly deletion evidence; data discovery scan

title: Sensitive authentication data not stored after authorisation
summary: SAD (full track; card verification code; PIN or PIN block) is not stored after authorisation even if encrypted; issuers storing SAD have a documented need.
typical_evidence: Data flow review; log and database scan showing no SAD

title: Display and copying of PAN restricted
summary: PAN is masked when displayed (show at most BIN and last four) unless a business need; copying or relocating PAN via remote access is prevented unless authorised.
typical_evidence: Screenshots of masked PAN; role list with full-PAN access

title: PAN secured wherever stored
summary: PAN rendered unreadable wherever stored (one-way hashes; truncation; tokens; strong cryptography); disk-level encryption alone is not enough for non-removable media.
typical_evidence: Encryption or tokenisation design; database column encryption settings

title: Cryptographic keys for stored account data secured
summary: Keys protecting stored account data are protected against disclosure and misuse; fewest custodians; stored securely.
typical_evidence: KMS or HSM configuration; key access policy

title: Key management processes
summary: Key management covers generation; distribution; storage; cryptoperiod changes; retirement; split knowledge where manual; prevention of unauthorised substitution; custodian acknowledgement.
typical_evidence: Key management procedure; rotation records; custodian acknowledgements

title: Protect data in transit: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for protecting CHD in transmission are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Encryption in transit policy

title: PAN protected with strong cryptography during transmission
summary: Strong cryptography for PAN over open public networks; certificates valid and not expired; inventory of trusted keys and certificates; PAN secured in end-user messaging.
typical_evidence: TLS configuration scan; certificate inventory; messaging policy

title: Malware protection: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for protecting systems from malware are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Anti-malware policy

title: Malware prevented or detected and addressed
summary: Anti-malware deployed on all components except those assessed as not at risk (with periodic evaluation).
typical_evidence: EDR or anti-malware console export; at-risk evaluation for excluded systems

title: Anti-malware active, maintained and monitored
summary: Kept current; periodic or real-time scans; removable media scanned; audit logs enabled; cannot be disabled by users without authorisation.
typical_evidence: EDR policy settings; update status; tamper protection

title: Anti-phishing mechanisms
summary: Processes and automated mechanisms detect and protect personnel against phishing.
typical_evidence: Email security configuration (DMARC; filtering); phishing training

title: Secure software: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for developing and maintaining secure systems and software are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Secure SDLC policy

title: Bespoke and custom software developed securely
summary: Developed to secure standards; developers trained at least annually; code reviewed before release; common attacks addressed.
typical_evidence: Secure coding training records; code review settings; SAST results

title: Security vulnerabilities identified and addressed
summary: Vulnerabilities identified and risk-ranked; inventory of bespoke and third-party software components; critical and high patches installed within one month.
typical_evidence: Vulnerability management procedure; SBOM or dependency inventory; patch records

title: Public-facing web applications protected
summary: Public-facing web apps protected against attacks by an automated technical solution (e.g. WAF); payment page scripts authorised, integrity-checked and inventoried.
typical_evidence: WAF configuration; payment page script inventory and integrity mechanism

title: Changes managed securely
summary: Change procedures (reason; security impact; approval; testing; back-out); pre-production separated from production; live PAN not used in pre-production; test data and accounts removed before release.
typical_evidence: Change records for sampled changes; environment separation; test data policy

title: Restrict access by need to know: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for restricting access are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Access control policy

title: Access appropriately defined and assigned
summary: Access model by job function; least privilege; approval by authorised personnel; user accounts and privileges reviewed at least every six months; application and system accounts reviewed.
typical_evidence: Role matrix; access approvals; six-monthly access review records

title: Access managed via access control systems
summary: Access control systems enforce need-to-know and deny by default.
typical_evidence: IAM configuration; default-deny policies

title: Identification and authentication: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for identifying users and authenticating access are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Identity and authentication policy

title: User identification and accounts managed
summary: Unique IDs; shared accounts only by exception; accounts added changed and removed with approval; terminated users revoked immediately; inactive accounts removed within 90 days; third-party remote access managed.
typical_evidence: IdP user export; joiner and leaver tickets; inactive account report

title: Strong authentication for users and administrators
summary: Authentication factors protected; passwords at least 12 characters (or 8 if not supported) with complexity; changed on suspicion; lockout after at most 10 attempts; session idle timeout of 15 minutes.
typical_evidence: Password and lockout policy export; session timeout settings

title: Multi-factor authentication into the CDE
summary: MFA for all non-console administrative access and for all access into the CDE; MFA for all remote network access.
typical_evidence: MFA enforcement exports (IdP; VPN; cloud console)

title: MFA systems configured to prevent misuse
summary: MFA cannot be bypassed; not susceptible to replay; requires at least two different factor types; success of all factors required.
typical_evidence: MFA configuration review

title: System and application accounts managed
summary: Interactive use of system or application accounts prevented or controlled; no hard-coded passwords; passwords changed periodically per targeted risk analysis.
typical_evidence: Service account inventory; secrets management; rotation records

title: Physical security: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for restricting physical access to CHD are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Physical security policy (often inherited from cloud provider)

title: Physical access controls manage entry
summary: Facility entry controls for systems in the CDE; monitoring of sensitive areas; network jacks and wireless access controlled; console access restricted.
typical_evidence: Cloud provider AOC (inherited); office access controls

title: Physical access for personnel and visitors authorised and managed
summary: Personnel and visitor access authorised; badges distinguished; access revoked on termination; visitor log retained at least three months.
typical_evidence: Visitor log; badge access records

title: Media with CHD securely stored, distributed and destroyed
summary: Media physically secured; classified; tracked when sent; inventoried; destroyed when no longer needed.
typical_evidence: Media handling procedure; destruction records

title: POI devices protected from tampering
summary: Point-of-interaction devices inventoried; inspected periodically for tampering and substitution; personnel trained.
typical_evidence: POI inventory and inspection logs (only if card-present)

title: Logging and monitoring: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for logging and monitoring are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Logging and monitoring policy

title: Audit logs implemented
summary: Audit logs capture user access to CHD; admin actions; access to audit logs; invalid access attempts; identification changes; log changes; object creation and deletion, with required details.
typical_evidence: Audit logging configuration; sample log entries

title: Audit logs protected
summary: Read access limited; logs protected from modification; promptly backed up to a central server; file integrity monitoring or change detection on logs.
typical_evidence: Log storage access policy; immutability or FIM settings

title: Audit logs reviewed
summary: Security events and critical system logs reviewed at least daily (automated mechanisms required); exceptions addressed.
typical_evidence: SIEM alert rules; review records

title: Audit log history retained
summary: Retain audit log history for at least 12 months with the most recent three months immediately available.
typical_evidence: Log retention settings (>=12 months)

title: Time synchronisation
summary: Time-synchronisation technology keeps clocks consistent; time data protected; settings changes logged.
typical_evidence: NTP configuration

title: Failures of critical security controls detected and addressed
summary: Failures of critical security control systems (NSCs; IDS; FIM; anti-malware; logging; access controls) are detected, alerted and responded to promptly.
typical_evidence: Alerting on control failures; incident records

title: Security testing: processes and roles
summary: Policies and procedures for testing security are documented, in use and known; roles assigned.
typical_evidence: Security testing policy

title: Wireless access points identified and monitored
summary: Authorised and unauthorised wireless access points detected quarterly; inventory of authorised APs.
typical_evidence: Quarterly wireless scans; AP inventory

title: Vulnerabilities identified, prioritised and addressed
summary: Internal vulnerability scans at least quarterly with authenticated scanning; external ASV scans quarterly with passing results; rescans after significant changes.
typical_evidence: Quarterly internal scan reports; ASV passing scans

title: Penetration testing
summary: Internal and external penetration tests at least annually and after significant changes; segmentation testing (six-monthly for service providers); findings corrected and retested.
typical_evidence: Penetration test reports; segmentation test; retest evidence

title: Intrusions and unexpected file changes detected
summary: IDS or IPS on CDE perimeter and critical points; change-detection on critical files with weekly comparisons.
typical_evidence: IDS or GuardDuty configuration; FIM configuration

title: Unauthorised changes on payment pages detected
summary: Change- and tamper-detection on payment pages as received by the consumer browser; evaluated at least weekly.
typical_evidence: Payment page monitoring tool configuration and alerts

title: Information security policy
summary: A comprehensive information security policy is established, published, reviewed at least annually and communicated; roles defined; a CISO or equivalent assigned.
typical_evidence: Approved policy with annual review; named security owner

title: Acceptable use policies
summary: Acceptable use policies for end-user technologies are documented and implemented.
typical_evidence: Acceptable use policy; acknowledgements

title: Risks formally identified, evaluated and managed
summary: Targeted risk analyses for requirements with flexible frequency; cryptographic cipher suites reviewed annually; hardware and software technologies reviewed annually.
typical_evidence: Targeted risk analyses; crypto inventory review; technology review

title: PCI DSS compliance managed
summary: Executive responsibility for protecting CHD and PCI DSS compliance; service providers review personnel compliance with tasks quarterly.
typical_evidence: Executive accountability record; quarterly reviews (service providers)

title: PCI DSS scope documented and validated
summary: Inventory of in-scope system components; scope confirmed at least annually and on significant change.
typical_evidence: Scope document; system inventory; annual scope confirmation

title: Security awareness education
summary: Formal awareness programme on hire and at least annually; covers phishing and social engineering; acknowledgements.
typical_evidence: Training records; content covering phishing

title: Personnel screened
summary: Potential personnel with CDE access are screened before hire within local law.
typical_evidence: Background check records for sampled hires

title: Third-party service provider risk managed
summary: List of TPSPs; written agreements acknowledging responsibility; due diligence before engagement; annual monitoring of PCI DSS compliance; responsibility matrix.
typical_evidence: TPSP list; agreements; AOCs collected annually; responsibility matrix

title: TPSPs support customers' compliance
summary: Service providers acknowledge responsibility for account data in writing and provide compliance and responsibility information on request.
typical_evidence: Customer agreement clauses; responsibility matrix (service providers only)

title: Incidents responded to immediately
summary: Incident response plan covering card data compromise; tested annually; 24x7 personnel; training; alerts from monitoring included; procedure for PAN found where unexpected.
typical_evidence: Incident response plan; annual test record; on-call roster

title: Multi-tenant providers protect customer environments
summary: Multi-tenant service providers logically separate customer environments and restrict customer access to their own environment.
typical_evidence: Tenant isolation design (multi-tenant service providers only)

title: Multi-tenant providers support logging and incident response
summary: Multi-tenant providers enable logging per customer and support forensic investigation and incident reporting.
typical_evidence: Per-tenant logging; incident support procedure (multi-tenant service providers only)

title: POI terminals using SSL or early TLS
summary: POI terminals using SSL or early TLS are confirmed not susceptible to known exploits.
typical_evidence: POI terminal TLS assessment (card-present only)

title: DESV: PCI DSS compliance programme
summary: Designated entities: executive responsibility and a charter for the PCI DSS compliance programme.
typical_evidence: Only if designated by a brand or acquirer

title: DESV: scope documented and validated
summary: Designated entities: scope validated quarterly and after changes; data discovery.
typical_evidence: Only if designated

title: DESV: PCI DSS incorporated into BAU
summary: Designated entities: failures of critical controls detected and responded to; BAU reviews.
typical_evidence: Only if designated

title: DESV: logical access controlled and managed
summary: Designated entities: user accounts and privileges reviewed at least every six months.
typical_evidence: Only if designated

title: DESV: suspicious events identified and responded to
summary: Designated entities: a methodology to identify attack patterns and respond.
typical_evidence: Only if designated
